objective.statement: Understand the Grade 4 Italian and French terms.
successCriteria: I know the terms of expression: affettuoso, amabile, appassionato, cantando, facile, con fuoco, nobilmente, sonoro.
I know the terms for changes of speed and fading: affrettando, calando, morendo, perdendosi, l'istesso tempo.
I know the words that point back or around: come prima, come sopra, quasi, sopra, sotto voce, niente, tempo giusto, presto possibile.

explanation.text: Grade 4 adds more Italian words for the way music should sound. Some describe character: affettuoso (tenderly), amabile (in a pleasant, amiable way), appassionato (with passion), cantando (in a singing style), facile (easily), con fuoco (with fire), nobilmente (nobly) and sonoro (with a full, resonant tone).

Some describe changes: affrettando (hurrying), calando (getting softer and usually slower), morendo (dying away) and perdendosi (fading away until lost). L'istesso tempo means 'at the same speed as before': the beat stays the same even when the time signature changes. Tempo giusto means in strict, exact time, and presto possibile means as fast as possible.

Others are small words that join with others: come prima (as before) and come sopra (as above), quasi (as if, almost like), sopra (above), sotto voce (in an undertone, very softly) and niente (nothing, as in 'fading to nothing').

music.textAlternative: A treble stave in 3/4 marked affettuoso: three falling crotchets, E, D and C.

explanation.caption: A direction printed above the first bar sets the character: here, affettuoso, tenderly.

explanation.text: Learn them in three groups: character (affettuoso ... sonoro), change (affrettando, calando, morendo, perdendosi ...), and joining words (come, quasi, sopra, sotto, niente).

music.textAlternative: A treble stave with three notes going down: E, D, C, for a passage marked morendo.

steps: Marked morendo, the music dies away.
Calando and perdendosi are close cousins: all fade.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 16 and First Steps Grade 4 section 15 (p. 103, read in the PDF), which states that its list is the Grade 4 list of the companion workbook. OPEN_QUESTIONS Q2: the official outline does not publish a term list, so these 21 terms are provisional and need teacher confirmation. Terms with (nearly) the same meaning (calando, morendo, perdendosi) are never offered as alternatives to one another and are never asked as 'which term means ...'. Grade 1-3 terms are never asked here, so no earlier-grade fact can earn Grade 4 credit.
